ApprovalDecideParams.description:
`approval/decide` params (tdd SS5.4): the decision. A standard SS3
command — requires the session loaded on this host, requires `commandId`,
durable intake before ack, value-identical replay.

feedback.description:
Free-text guidance delivered to the model with the denial. Only valid
on choices with `acceptsFeedback`. Never persisted in the durable
audit record (live steer only), so it is absent from
`approval/resolved` (tdd SS5.4). Omitted and explicit `null` both
mean "no feedback" (#23468).

requirementId.description:
Must equal the approval's `currentRequirementId`. The multi-stage race
guard: a decision aimed at stage 1 can never accidentally satisfy
stage 2, and a stale value is -32053 (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalDecideResult.description:
`approval/decide` result (tdd SS5.4). Admission-ack rules still apply: the
authoritative outcome is `approval/resolved` / `approval/updated` on the
view stream.

approvalId.description: The approval this decision was applied to.

terminal.description:
`false` when the choice satisfied a stage but further requirements
remain (the approval stays pending and an updated `approval/request`
follows); `true` when this decision produced the terminal
`DecisionApplied` (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalListPendingParams.description:
`approval/listPending` params (tdd SS5.7): the pull dual of the re-issued
requests. A log-fold read — no lease, works on loaded and unloaded
sessions, never subscribes.

ApprovalListPendingResult.description:
`approval/listPending` result (tdd SS5.7). Ordering is by opening
`viewCursor`; empty arrays when nothing is pending. The result is
point-in-time — to act on it race-safely, `approval/decide` carries the
`requirementId` guard regardless of how the client learned the state.

approvals.description:
Exactly the `approval/request` params of tdd SS5.3, one per pending
approval.

userInputs.description:
Exactly the `userInput/request` params of tdd SS5.10, one per pending
prompt.

ApprovalMode.description:
The approval enforcement modes (tdd SS5.12, camelCased
`ApprovalBackendMode`). **Closed** by design (D-006, select-never-create):
a client selects a preconfigured mode and can never construct one;
widening this enum is a deliberate, gate-visible protocol change.

ApprovalModeApplyOutcome.description:
Whether a mode change did anything (tdd SS5.12), mirroring
`ApprovalReconfigureApplyOutcome`. Apply failures are `commandRejected`.

ApprovalModeSource.description:
How an approval mode took effect (tdd SS5.12, the effective-mode
projection's `source` vocabulary). Open.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

ApprovalRequirementRef.description: Approval-stage token carried in SS5 params and stale-requirement errors.

ApprovalResolutionSummary.description: Winning terminal returned to a losing `approval/decide` command.

ApprovalResolvedParams.description: `approval/resolved` params: the first durable terminal decision.

decidedAt.description:
The decision time as RFC3339, projected from the durable
`DecisionApplied` record's own stamp (ADR 45450 D3): optional on the
wire so decoders tolerate its absence, always populated by current
hosts.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

ApprovalSubagentOrigin.description:
Child (native subagent) provenance for an approval projected onto the
PARENT session's approval plane (#36182 / ADR 36182): identifies the
originating child run/agent so a client can attribute the prompt. Omitted
(`skip_serializing_if`) on the parent's own approvals, so pre-existing
parent frames stay byte-identical.

childRunId.description: The child run that parked on this approval.

childSessionId.description: The child session stream id whose records carry this approval.

subagentId.description:
The originating child's subagent id, from the parent session's
durable subagent control records.

ApprovalSubject.description:
Open approval subject union. Unknown kinds are rendered generically and
never auto-approved by clients (tdd SS5.2).

kind.description: Open discriminator: `shell | fileAccess | network | unixSocket | process | tool`.

ApprovalUpdatedParams.description: `approval/updated` params: the refreshed pending view plus one change.

subagentOrigin.description:
Present only for a child (native subagent) approval projected onto
the parent session's plane (ADR 36182); parent-own approvals omit it.

AttentionFlag.description:
One attention flag (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D3): a pending server-initiated
request class parked on the session. Open on the wire — clients MUST
ignore unknown values; future attention kinds are additive.

BackgroundInitiator.description:
Who durably backgrounded a task (tdd SS4.5.5,
`TaskBackgroundedInitiator`). Open — runtime vocabulary.

BranchState.description: The latest branch observation in the snapshot (tdd SS4.6.4, SS4.9.1).

branch.description: The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation.

vcs.description: The detected version-control system; absent when none was detected.

CapabilityName.description:
A grantable capability name (SS1.4.4). Open: the reserved `rawLog` entry
joins this domain as an additive open-enum extension when SS6 un-defers
(#13929, Scenario 5 AS-3) — closed would make that a retype.

ClientCapabilities.description:
The client's requested capability posture (SS1.4.1). Every member
defaults; an absent `capabilities` object means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Opt into experimental methods, fields, and variants (default `false`).

requestedCapabilities.description:
Names from the capability registry. Unknown entries are not an error
and simply do not appear in `grantedCapabilities` — which is why this
is a list of free strings rather than of registry names.

userInputDialogs.description:
Whether this client can render a `userInput/request` dialog and answer
it (SS5.10). **Absent means capable** (D-047): a client that predates
the member keeps today's contract, so no existing client changes its
handshake. `false` makes the host withhold `userInput/request` toward
this client — the D-027 additive-optional-field + withheld-method
convention.

Deliberately NOT a `requestedCapabilities` name: that registry records
operations a host GRANTS (SS1.4.4), and whether a client can draw a
dialog is a fact about the client, never a privilege the host hands
out.

ClientInfo.description:
Client identification inside `initialize` params (SS1.4.1). Diagnostics
and telemetry attribution only; never an authority claim (SS1.10).

CodeModeLanguage.description:
The language a Code Mode cell ran in (ADR 42727 D2). Open: values are
lowercase VS Code language identifiers, and only `javascript` (the V8
engine) is minted today.

CodeModeOutputSpan.description:
One public-output span inside the item's `visibleOutput` (ADR 42727 D3).

Offsets index the UTF-8 encoding of the **decoded** `visibleOutput`
string, never the JSON-escaped wire text; both ends fall on code-point
boundaries; named and measured like `item/readOutput`'s byte range.

lengthBytes.description: Length of the span, in bytes.

offsetBytes.description: Start of the span, in bytes.

CodeModeOutputStream.description:
What a Code Mode output span's bytes are (ADR 42727 D3). Open: each
engine mints its own values.

CodeModeReceipt.description:
Code Mode's `details` payload (ADR 42727 D2/D3).

Every member is absent when it does not apply, never `null`; an empty
`outputSpans` list is never served.

cellItemId.description:
`wait` only, when the producer resolved it: the `itemId` of the
`execute` item that started the cell.

language.description:
`execute`, and `wait` when the producer resolved the originating
execute: the language the cell ran in.

outputSpans.description:
The public cell-output spans, ascending and non-overlapping; absent
when there is no cell body or a hook rewrote the served body.

sourceArg.description:
`execute` only: the top-level key of the item's `args` object whose
value is the cell source. A pointer, never source bytes.

CommandAcceptedResult.description:
The uniform SS3.1.2 command acknowledgement: admission only, never an
outcome. `session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`; every other command
answers `"accepted"`.

status.description: `"accepted"` for every admitted command (SS3.1.2; closed vocabulary).

CommandAckStatus.description:
The ack-status vocabulary (`tdd.md` SS3.1/SS3.1.2): `"accepted"` for every
admitted command; `session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`. Closed:
SS3.1.2 names exactly these two values, so SDK clients get a discriminated
type and validation catches a wrong status (PR #21550 review) — and a
client that received a third value would have been told nothing it can act
on, unlike [`TurnStartDisposition`], where "acked, not otherwise
classified" is a usable reading.

CommandStatus.description:
The SS3.1.2 ack `status`: `accepted` for every admitted command.
`session/compact` is the one method that may additionally answer `noop`
([`crate::method::runtime::CompactStatus`]); no other command uses another
status (tdd SS3.1.2).

CompactStatus.description:
`session/compact`'s ack status (tdd SS3.7): the one method that may answer
`noop` in addition to the SS3.1.2 `accepted`. A noop is a success, not an
error, and it is durably settled like any other outcome.

CompactionOutcome.description: Compaction outcome (tdd SS4.5.10, the SS3.7 vocabulary). Open.

CompactionTrigger.description: What initiated a compaction (tdd SS4.5.10). Open.

ComputerUseBlockedApp.description: One row of the Settings blocked-apps list.

bundleId.description: The app's bundle ID, or the family prefix when `prefix` is true.

locked.description: A built-in block, which Settings cannot remove (ADR 630 D18.8).

prefix.description:
A built-in family row: it blocks every bundle ID that starts with
`bundleId`. Omitted means false; only locked rows are prefixes.

ComputerUseChoice.description:
A capability dropdown's value (ADR 630 D18.4). **Open**: the read result
carries it, so an older client tolerates a value it does not know.

ComputerUsePermission.description: One macOS permission as setup last saw it. **Open**, like the phase.

blockedApps.description:
The user's blocks in the order they were added, then the built-in
blocks when `showBuiltIns` asked for them.

computerControl.description:
The computer-control dropdown, as it applies: `ask` while the stored
blocked-apps list can't be read (ADR 630 D18.4).

screenshots.description: The screenshots dropdown, under the same rule.

showBuiltIns.description:
Also list the built-in blocks as locked rows (the D18.8 toggle).
Omitted means false.

ComputerUseSettingsUpdateParams.description:
`computerUseSettings/update` params: a patch. Omitted members are left
alone; the whole patch applies or none of it does.

blockApps.description:
Bundle IDs to add to the user's blocked apps. A built-in block is
refused: it is already blocked.

unblockApps.description:
Bundle IDs to remove from the user's blocked apps. Only the user's own
entries can be removed; a built-in block stays.

sessionId.description: The session whose setup state changed.

ComputerUseSetupPhase.description:
Where the session's setup stands: `cua_setup`'s state codes, camelCase.
**Open**: a result vocabulary, so an older client tolerates a new state.

sessionId.description: The session whose setup to read.

commandId.description: The client's id for this command.

sessionId.description: The session whose setup to start.

ComputerUseSetupState.description:
The session's setup state: the result of both methods and the
`computerUseSetup/changed` payload's `state`.

inputMonitoring.description: Input Monitoring: computer use is ready without it; some actions need it.

message.description: The sentence `cua_setup` gives the user for this answer.

refused.description: The `cua_setup` refusal code when the call was refused, verbatim.

ContextPressureLevel.description:
Context pressure level (tdd SS4.6.6): hard threshold first, both
inclusive `>=`. Open.

ContextUsage.description:
The SS4.9.1 snapshot `contextUsage` block: the latest
`(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple; the snapshot member is
`null` until the fold's generation chain holds a tracked anchor AND the
current basis is present (absent is never fabricated).

usedTokens.description: Counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported fact.

windowTokens.description: The effective context-window size; absent when the basis has no limit.

CronReceipt.description:
Cron's `details` payload (ADR 42728 D2, thirteenth directive).

Every field a family owns lives here, under the container's one
`details` key, rather than flat beside the discriminators — ADR 43399 D5
as amended. Each is a **bounded machine fact**: scalars, short
identifiers and a small fixed-shape array of those.

jobId.description:
Cron `create` and `delete`: the job id. On `delete`'s `missing` arm
this is the caller's own id echoed back under ADR 43399 D1's declared
echo — that arm has no server-side subject to name.

Also the field ADR 42728 D4's D8 declaration names as conveying the
hidden fact on the declared `created` + `cancelled` pairing: a job row
was committed and will fire.

jobs.description:
Cron `list`: the served jobs in server order, `active` and `firing`
rows only.

nextFireAtMs.description:
Cron `create` (`created`, `duplicate`): absolute epoch-milliseconds of
the job's next scheduled fire (the existing job's on `duplicate`,
ADR 42728 D2).

CronReceiptJob.description:
One row of the Cron `list` receipt's `jobs` array (ADR 42728 D2).

Server order, and **`active` + `firing` rows only** — the owner's
`Serve active+firing only` directive. A small fixed-shape array of
scalars, which is what keeps it inside D5's bounded-machine-fact rule.

nextFireAtMs.description: Absolute epoch-milliseconds of the job's next scheduled fire.

CumulativeCost.description:
Server-computed session cost member of [`CumulativeTokenUsage`]
(tdd SS4.6.5, Amendment #41610 FR-41610-2/3).

partial.description:
True when at least one leg lacked price data — clients render
`(partial)`.

usd.description: Estimated USD total, finite and non-negative.

CumulativeTokenUsage.description:
Session running totals of counted-once usage (tdd SS4.6.5).

Amendment #41610: the cache splits and server-computed `cost` join the
counters. The counters stay accumulate-only; `cost` is the documented
exception — it may move either way on price re-adoption and is labeled
estimate (INV-41610-1). `Copy` was dropped for the `cost` member.

cacheReadTokens.description:
Cache-read tokens, session total (FR-41610-1): saturating sum of
the per-completion splits; an absent split contributes 0.
Additive-optional: absent on the wire reads as 0 and zero totals
are omitted, so pre-feature bytes decode and re-encode identically.

cacheWriteTokens.description:
Cache-write tokens, session total (FR-41610-1). Additive-optional
like the read split.

cost.description:
Server-computed session cost (FR-41610-2): `None` (wire-absent)
when no leg is priced — clients omit the row. Additive-optional:
absent reads as unpriced.

EffectiveApprovalModeState.description:
The effective approval-mode projection (`EffectiveApprovalModeState`,
tdd SS5.12): the same object `session/setApprovalMode` returns as
`effectiveMode` and the `Session` object carries as `approvalMode`.

lastCommandId.description: The command that last set it; `null` when no command did.

EffectiveModel.description: The latest effective-model fact in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1).

providerId.description: The selected provider; `null` when the selection names none.

ErrorData.description:
The optional `error.data` object (SS1.6). All members additive-optional;
`kind` is always present when `data` is.

alignedNextOffset.description:
The next provable UTF-8 boundary on a misaligned text-media
`item/readOutput` read (`-32602` `invalidParams`, FR-016b/D-17214-2):
absent when no boundary is provable from the stored bytes ahead.

anchor.description:
The rejected anchor value on `notFound`/`missingAnchor` and the
`-32042` boundary arms (SS4.7.3, SS4.11); on `-32042` it is served
as an explicit `null` when the request named no concrete anchor
(spec 208 FM-005).

availability.description:
The stored output's availability on `outputUnavailable` — the durable
`ToolOutputAvailability` value, read-time-derived when the durable
record still says `available` (SS4.5.5; spec 208 FM-008).

capability.description:
The missing capability, on `capabilityRequired` errors. Typed on the
grantable registry, so `rawLog` is outside the v1 domain and joins it
as an additive open-enum extension when SS6 un-defers (TEST-009).

capacity.description: The configured command-admission bound, on `backpressured` errors.

commandId.description:
The rejected command's identifier, on `commandRejected` errors. The
ratified v1 contract pairs it with `reason`
(specs/13929-msp-activation/tdd.md SS3.6 admission-failure table and
its `-32030` example), so a client can settle the exact command it
sent without parsing the message string.

earliestCursor.description:
The oldest servable view position on `viewTruncated` (`-32040`,
SS4.11); served as an explicit `null` when nothing before the head
is servable — the null is present on the wire, never a dropped key
(spec 208 FM-005 / Scenario 6.2).

itemId.description:
The item whose stored output was requested, on the `item/readOutput`
arms (`notFound`, `outputUnavailable`, and the misaligned-offset
`invalidParams`).

kind.description: The stable camelCase category clients branch on.

latestBoundaryCursor.description:
The latest installed boundary's view cursor on the `-32042` arms —
always present in the `-32042` JSON and explicitly `null` when no
boundary exists (SS4.11, FM-004).

limitBytes.description: The exceeded byte limit, on `inputTooLarge` errors.

name.description:
The rejected marketplace name on `marketplaceNotFound` (`-32034`,
SS3.29.7) and `marketplaceAlreadyExists` (`-32036`, SS3.29.2); the
rejected plugin name on `pluginNotFound` (`-32035`, SS3.29.1).

outputRef.description: The requested `outputRef.id`, on the same `item/readOutput` arms.

reason.description:
Failure detail vocabulary (e.g. `"missingAnchor"` on `notFound` for a
missing view-cursor anchor).

retryable.description:
Whether retrying can succeed (e.g. `overloaded`). When present,
overrides the error table row's `retryable` default for this code.

seedFallbackReason.description:
Why the branch seed did not use a checkpoint, on the same arms:
one of `no_usable_checkpoint`, `unsupported_checkpoint_shape`,
`checkpoint_has_model_visible_tail`, `checkpoint_missing_suffix`;
absent when the seed used a checkpoint or no fallback was recorded.

seedPath.description:
The branch-seed path the host read before rejecting, on
branch-validation rejections (`session/fork`, `session/sideChat`:
the `forkBoundaryInvalid`, `commandRejected` and `sessionNotFound`
arms; SS2.5.3, SS2.5.7; #51365): one of `runtime_checkpoint_tail`,
`runtime_full_replay`, `legacy_session_data` — the durable
branch-seed vocabulary, so the client cites the real seed decision
instead of guessing at a stale binary.

selector.description: The rejected skill selector on `skillNotFound` (`-32032`, SS3.22.4).

sessionId.description: Session identity on errors whose lookup is session-scoped.

uploadId.description: The rejected upload id on `uploadNotFound` (`-32038`, SS3.33).

userInputId.description: User-input prompt identity on SS5.10 errors.

viewCursor.description: The blocked view position on `pageEventTooLarge` errors.

ErrorKind.description:
A stable `error.data.kind` category (SS1.6): camelCase, the value clients
branch on. Open: SS2–SS5 lanes add kinds additively as their methods land
(Appendix B already registers them), and the spec's edge-case rule makes a
new `kind` additive only because this domain is declared open.

ErrorObject.description: The `error` member of an error response (SS1.2 §2.4).

code.description:
Registry code (Appendix B). Typed as a plain integer on the wire; the
value domain is the registry below (INV-018).

message.description: Human-readable message. Never a branch point (SS1.6).

ErrorResponse.description:
An error response frame (SS1.2 §2.4). Exactly one of `result` or `error`
appears on a response; this type is the `error` half.

id.description:
Echo of the request id; `null` **only** for an unrecoverable parse
error whose offending id could not be recovered (SS1.3). Always
serialized, so `None` renders as `null` rather than being omitted —
required-but-nullable (see [`require_nullable_id`]).

FeedbackClassification.description:
`feedback/submit` classification (tdd SS3.25): the four TUI classes in
camelCase wire spelling. **Closed**: a client-selected param
vocabulary (#22785 E2).

FeedbackSubmitOutcome.description:
`feedback/submit` result `outcome` (tdd SS3.25): how one confirmed
submit resolved, mirroring the TUI `FeedbackSubmitOutcome` taxonomy.
**Open**: a server-produced result vocabulary (#22785 E2) — an older
client reading a newer value it does not know follows the open-enum
tolerance rule instead of rejecting it.

FeedbackSubmitParams.description:
`feedback/submit` params (tdd SS3.25): mirrors the TUI confirm-time
`FeedbackRequest`. The call itself is the explicit confirm.

attachSessionRecord.description:
Consent to attach the session record; honored only for
`bug`/`badResult` with `session_id` present. `true` with
`with_files: false`, with a non-`bug`/`badResult` classification,
or without `session_id` is `invalidParams` (F4, F8).
Defaults to `false`.

clientArtifactsPath.description:
An absolute same-host path to a client-packed bundle, admitted
only as a regular file under a size cap.

note.description: The user report text (required; non-empty for `bug`).

sessionId.description:
Names the session this call is about when present (F8,
superseding F3): the bundle lands in that session's dir. Names a
session this host owns. When absent, the bundle lands in the
host-level feedback folder and the `session_id` tag is omitted.

bundlePath.description: The host-local absolute path of the always-written local bundle.

cause.description:
The failure cause on the `failed`, `acceptedWithoutReceipt`,
`trackingFailed`, and `trackingUncertain` arms.

localTracingNote.description: The consent-vs-reality local-tracing note, kept for display.

retryAfterMs.description: The effective retry delay in milliseconds, on `rateLimited`.

sessionNote.description: The consent-vs-reality session note, kept for display.

sessionRecordAttached.description: Whether the consented session record rode at all.

sessionRecordTruncated.description: Whether the consented session record rode shortened to fit.

taskId.description: The internal receipt-Task id once that Task succeeds.

uploadId.description:
The intake's accept id — always present on the `uploaded` arm,
optional on `trackingFailed`/`trackingUncertain`; never fabricated
on `recorded`.

ForkCutPoint.description:
Where a fork cuts the source history (tdd SS2.5.3). Turn ids are used
instead of counts because ids stay stable across compaction and concurrent
appends while indices do not.

lastTurnId.description:
The last completed turn to copy, inclusive. Naming an in-progress or
unknown turn fails `forkBoundaryInvalid`.

ForkProvenance.description:
Fork provenance folded from the durable `session.fork.created` record
(`ForkProvenance`, tdd SS2.4).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `session/fork` that created it.

cutCursor.description:
An **opaque provenance string** preserved verbatim from the durable
record. Display-only — not one of the SS6.2 cursor families: clients
MUST NOT parse it and no method accepts it (tdd SS2.4).

cutExplicit.description: Whether the fork named an explicit cut point.

sessionId.description: The source session this fork was cut from.

Goal.description:
The session goal block (tdd SS4.6.2, mirrors the runtime's goal state,
camelCased). `status` and `percentComplete` are carried **verbatim** —
out-of-contract status strings and >100 percents pass through; display
clamping is the renderer's job.

status.description:
Goal status, verbatim from the durable goal state (free string by
design: out-of-contract values pass through).

GoalClearParams.description:
`goal/clear` params (tdd SS3.18). An `objective` here is an unknown field
and rejects `-32602 invalidParams` — the bare verbs carry exactly this
pair.

GoalCommandResult.description:
The shared SS3.18 goal ack, admission-only: all five verbs answer this
one shape (the tdd's "Shared contract"), differing only in when `turnId`
is present.

turnId.description:
Present by exactly the four SS3.18 result cases: an idle wake carries
the fresh goal turn's id; a busy `set`/`edit`/`resume` carries the
admission-time active turn's id (a routing fact, not a delivery
promise); `pause`/`clear` never carry it; an idle admission whose
resulting goal is not unfinished parks the notification and carries
none. **Additive-optional**: absent means "no turn named", never
fabricated.

GoalEditParams.description:
`goal/edit` params (tdd SS3.18): replace the current goal's objective.
Same shape as `goal/set`; the verbs differ in their `missing_goal`
precondition, not their payload.

objective.description: The replacement objective; same trim/non-empty rule as `goal/set`.

GoalSetParams.description: `goal/set` params (tdd SS3.18): set the session's goal objective.

objective.description:
The objective text; required, non-empty after Unicode-whitespace trim
(the trimmed text is the payload). Empty-after-trim is
`-32602 invalidParams` (tdd SS3.18).

HistoryMode.description:
What history a lifecycle result actually served (tdd SS2.5.2). Open on the
client side: report-what-was-served means a client treats an unknown mode
as "page it yourself".

HistoryNoneReason.description:
Why a result served `history.mode: "none"` — spec 208 FM-005's typed
unavailability (tdd SS2.5.2; D-050). Open on the client side: an absent
(older server) or unknown (newer server) value decodes conservatively as
an unknown reason, and `viewCursor` text never substitutes for it
(spec 208 INV-19734-1).

HistoryPreference.description:
The `history` request preference of `session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.2). The
forced values downgrade `anchored` → `inline` → `snapshot` → `none`; under
`auto` the full rung order is anchoredSnapshot → inline → snapshot →
elided snapshot → none.

enabled.description:
The row's own switch (tdd SS3.26.1). Non-enabled rows are
included as `false`, never dropped.

event.description: The event the handler runs on (ADR 33398 D7 item 2).

handlerKind.description: Where the handler comes from (ADR 33398 D7 item 1).

key.description: The handler key (config key or plugin hook id).

HookEventName.description:
Hook event names (tdd SS3.26.1, ADR 33398 D7 item 2): the
lowercase-first-letter spelling of every `HookEventKind::all()`
variant. Open (server-produced result vocabulary, the #22785
enum-openness rule): a future event value is additive.

HookHandlerKind.description:
A hook row's origin (tdd SS3.26.1, ADR 33398 D7 item 1): the config
`HookSourceKind` values plus plugin-contributed. Open (server-produced
result vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future origin is
additive.

HookListParams.description:
`hook/list` params (tdd SS3.26.1). Per-session because hook scope
follows the session's workspace and plugin state.

HookListResult.description:
`hook/list` result (tdd SS3.26.1): one row per installed handler per
event — a `ResolvedHookHandler` carries one event, and grouping would
lose matcher/command identity (ADR 33398 D7 item 1).

hooks.description:
The session's installed hook rows (tdd SS3.26.1 promises the
set, not an order).

HookRunStatus.description:
`hookRun` durable outcome (tdd SS4.5.11). Open: new outcomes are
additive, and clients MUST render unknown values generically.

IfBusy.description:
Disposition when a turn is already running (tdd SS3.2). The wire default
is `queue`: an SDK caller who has not looked at session state should not
silently mutate an in-flight turn.

capabilities.description: Capability posture; absent means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Echo of the effective negotiated experimental setting.

grantedCapabilities.description:
Subset of the requested capabilities, plus policy-implicit grants.
Fixed for the connection lifetime (INV-009).

museHome.description: Absolute path of the muse home directory.

schema.description: Envelope schema version and stable-surface fingerprint.

sessionDurability.description:
Whether this host persists its sessions (SS2.13). Optional so the
addition is additive under SS1.5.4; a v1 host always sends it, and a
client reads absent as `durable` because no server that omits it has
the ephemeral profile.

userAgent.description: Exact user-agent string presented to upstream model providers.

Item.description:
One transcript item at one revision (tdd SS4.4.1 common fields plus the
per-kind fields of SS4.5.2–4.5.11, all optional and owned by the kind
their doc names). `item/started`, `item/updated`, and `item/completed`
carry the full object; `item/delta` appends to it by field path.

approvalId.description:
`toolCall`: the approval that gated this call (tdd SS5); join key for
the approval view events.

args.description:
`toolCall`: the model-authored argument JSON, **verbatim**; clients
parse. Verbatim keeps the fold byte-deterministic and survives
model-emitted almost-JSON (tdd SS4.5.5).

attachments.description:
`userMessage`: image attachment metadata only — base64 payloads are
not echoed back on the view (tdd SS4.5.2).

background.description:
`toolCall`: `true` once the task was durably backgrounded; delivered
via `item/updated`.

backgroundInitiator.description:
`toolCall`: who backgrounded the task; absent on pre-split records —
never inferred (tdd SS4.5.5).

blocking.description:
`reminderChild`: `true` when this child is a blocking reminder (it holds
the turn open until it settles); absent otherwise, never `false` (ADR
41191 D4). The status word stays off the wire; clients name the
reminder from `reminderAgentId`.

childPromptRefs.description:
`workflow`: one `outputRef`-shaped link per recorded child spawn
with an objective (`kind: "workflow_child_prompt"`), fetched via
`item/readOutput` (tdd SS4.5.8/SS4.7.4, #45449).

childSessionId.description:
`subagent`/`reminderChild`: the child's own session id, readable via
`session/read`/`view/page` — child transcript drill-down without a
second protocol (tdd SS4.5.7).

childSessionLogPath.description:
`reminderChild`: parent-session-dir-relative child log path; absent
when no filesystem log.

children.description:
`workflow`: folded per-child state, keyed by `(childId, attempt)`,
re-emitted whole on every change — the item `revision` is the
ordering guard (tdd SS4.5.8).

commandId.description:
`userMessage`/`userShell`: the submitting command — multi-client UIs
de-duplicate their local echo on it.

controlStatus.description:
`subagent`: camelCased `SubagentControlStatus` (open enum); `status`
stays the generic item vocabulary.

declaredPhase.description:
`workflow`: the run-level declared-phase label — the last `Phase`
detail-row label of the reconciled projection; terminal-only, absent
while live (tdd SS4.5.8, #45449).

displayText.description:
`userMessage`: presentation form (tdd SS3.2); absent when the client
sent none.

durationMs.description:
`userShell`/`subagent`: observed wall-clock duration. `workflow`: the
run's wall time from launch to reconciliation, set only on the
settling `item/completed` — never a sum of child durations.

event.description: `hookRun`: the hook event in Q2 camelCase vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.11).

exitCode.description: `userShell`: the process exit code, when it exited by code.

exitSignal.description:
`userShell`: the terminating signal NUMBER, when signalled (e.g. 9) —
the durable payload verbatim; nothing maps numbers to names, and the
fold never invents one.

failureKind.description:
`toolCall`: machine-readable failure class (`TaskFailureKind`,
snake_case verbatim — durable runtime vocabulary, the SS1.6 casing
exemption).

fallbackText.description:
Server-provided one-line human summary any kind MAY carry, for
generic rendering of kinds a client does not recognize; new kinds
SHOULD carry it during their first release cycle (tdd SS4.10).

finalSummary.description:
`workflow`: the human terminal summary projected from the reconciled
Launch envelope, bounded at the 64 KiB surface budget; terminal-only
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449).

itemId.description:
Bare UUIDv7; the item's identity across its whole lifecycle. Identity
rule (tdd SS4.4.1): the task id for task-backed kinds
(`toolCall`, `subagent`), the pre-minted commit `message_id` for
delta-streamed kinds (`agentMessage`, `reasoning`), and the opening
durable record's event id for everything else. Opaque to clients.

kind.description:
The item kind (open enum): clients MUST render unknown kinds
generically — kind name plus `status` plus `fallbackText` (tdd
SS4.10).

message.description: `workflow`: the reconciled terminal message, set on completion.

modelVisibleContent.description:
`toolCall`: rich content the model saw beyond text; base64 is not
inlined on the view (tdd SS4.5.5).

objective.description:
`subagent`: objective as spawned, bounded on the wire at the 64 KiB
retained-text budget (tdd SS4.5.4, ADR 35691 D9); a cut sets
`truncated`. The durable record stays verbatim.

outputRef.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: stored-output reference; fetch the full bytes
via `item/readOutput` (served by #208).

patchRef.description:
`toolCall`: stored structured-patch reference (`kind: "tool_patch"`,
`mediaType: "application/json"`); the body is fetched via
`item/readOutput` with `patchRef.id`, and the ref survives the
SS2.5.2 elided-snapshot rung exactly like `outputRef` without ever
being an elision trigger (tdd SS2.5.2, SS4.5.5; #33025).

patchSummary.description:
`toolCall`: server-authored edit-family diff summary (#33025)
— always beside `patchRef`; absent = no diff available (tdd SS4.5.5).

paused.description:
`workflow`: `true` only while a durable pause fact is in force for
the run's generation; absent otherwise, never `false` (tdd SS4.5.8,
ADR 45437 D2; the fold sets it on pause commit and clears it on
resume-commit supersession or the generation's terminal).

providerItemId.description:
`reasoning`: provider reasoning item id (e.g. `rs_...`), for
provider-side correlation.

reason.description:
`compaction`: noop/failure reason, verbatim (snake_case durable
vocabulary, e.g. `"no_compactable_history"`). `hookRun`: terminal-only
capped terminal reason (tdd SS4.5.11).

recordedAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of the item's driving durable record. Absent on
ephemeral-opened items until first durable re-emission (tdd SS4.4.1).

retracted.description:
`userMessage`: `true` after an accepted retract (tdd SS4.5.1);
re-emitted via `item/updated`.

revision.description:
Integer >= 1, strictly monotonic per item; apply rule is
replace-iff-higher. `item/delta` never bumps it (tdd SS4.4.1).

runStatus.description:
`hookRun`: terminal-only durable outcome; stays `blocked` when the
item settles `rejected` (tdd SS4.5.11).

sideSessionId.description:
`sideChat`: the side's own session id, readable via
`session/read`/`view/page` — drill-down without a second protocol
(tdd SS4.5.13; ADR 45435 D3).

status.description:
Open enum; terminal = anything other than `"inProgress"`. Unknown
values MUST be treated as terminal-unknown and rendered generically
(tdd SS4.4.1).

statusAttempt.description:
`toolCall`: the latest external-attempt facet, field-for-field —
countdown inputs the client renders the tick from; absent when the
latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusChildren.description:
`toolCall`: the latest child-summary facet, field-for-field; absent
when the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusHealth.description:
`toolCall`: the latest health facet, field-for-field; absent when
the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusLine.description:
`toolCall`: the task's visible latest-status line — the latest
`Status` message through the shared detail normalization; absent
when no status folded or nothing displayable remains (tdd SS4.5.5,
#45448).

statusPhase.description:
`toolCall`: the latest detail's phase row, verbatim; absent when the
latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusProgress.description:
`toolCall`: the latest progress facet, field-for-field; absent when
the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

statusStep.description:
`toolCall`: the latest active-step facet, field-for-field; absent
when the latest detail carries none (tdd SS4.5.5, #45448).

steered.description:
`userMessage`: `true` when injected mid-turn via `turn/steer` or
`ifBusy: "steer"`; absent otherwise.

stopAvailable.description:
`workflow`: display-only stop affordance — `true` while the run is
open, `false` once settled; stopping rides `workflow/cancel`
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449). Authorizes nothing.

summarizedThrough.description:
`compaction`: opaque provenance string naming the compaction
boundary. A compaction-anchored read anchor since D-029 (2026-08-12):
accepted by `session/resume` and `view/page` (wire shape and
validation are the #208 lane's). Still opaque — clients relay it,
never parse it (tdd SS4.5.10).

summary.description:
`reasoning`: one entry per summary part; part *n* streams via
`item/delta` field `"summary.n"` (part boundary = index change).

text.description:
`userMessage`: the prompt text as submitted. `agentMessage`: the
accumulated reply, streamed via `item/delta` field `"text"`.
`reasoning`: raw committed reasoning text where the provider exposes
it (never streamed in v1, tdd SS4.5.4).

tokenBudget.description:
`workflow`: the run's launch token budget, set from the launch fact
(tdd SS4.5.8, #45449); absent when the launch carried none.

tokensAfter.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot after, when measured.

tokensBefore.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot before, when measured.

toolReceipt.description:
`toolCall`: the shared semantic receipt — what the operation did, as
machine-readable fact (ADR 43399 D1, tdd SS4.5.5). Optional and
additive: absence is always valid and is never an error (D3). When
present, a server serves the **same** receipt on every item path —
`item/completed`, `view/page`, seeded snapshots and resume (D3).
Observation only; carries no control authority (D4), and no field in
it enters model-visible content (D7).

truncated.description:
`true` when the server's per-surface text budget saturated a streamed
surface (`agentMessage.text`, `reasoning.summary[*]`,
`toolCall.visibleOutput`, `userShell.visibleOutput`), or cut a
`subagent` surface (`objective`, `fallbackText`, `result.summary`,
`result.text`). On a `subagent` item the flag is item-level and never
cleared: once any of those four is cut, every later update keeps it,
even when `result.text` arrives whole (ADR 35691 D9). The durable full
text remains in the log (tdd SS4.5.4).

turnId.description:
The owning turn (== the submitting `commandId` for fresh turns, tdd
SS3.1.4). `null` only for `userShell` — the one kind outside a turn
(tdd SS4.5.6).

usage.description:
`subagent`: **transitive** observed usage — the child and its own
descendants; updated in place, absent until first observation; never
folded into `session/tokenUsage.cumulative` (tdd SS4.6.5).

visibleOutput.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: bounded transcript-visible result text
(budget per tdd SS4.5.4); streams via `item/delta` field `"output"`.

workflowRunId.description:
`subagent`/`workflow`: the owning durable workflow run id (opaque
string — not a UUID family).

ItemCompletedParams.description:
`item/completed` params (tdd SS4.3): the item reached its terminal state
— the authoritative final object. Always cites a durable `sourceRange`
(tdd SS4.2). Clients MUST accept `item/completed` for an `itemId` they
never saw `item/started` for (single-shot kinds; after a gap fill; tdd
SS4.4.1).

item.description: The full item at its terminal revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemDeltaParams.description:
`item/delta` params (tdd SS4.3.1): a UTF-8-safe streaming append to an
open item's field. Ephemeral-sourced by definition: this params object
has **no** `sourceRange` member at all (spec 14653 INV-009 — the schema
enforces the exemption). Deltas never bump `revision`.

delta.description:
The appended text; concatenation of a field path's deltas in cursor
order equals that field's value on `item/completed` unless the
surface saturated (spec 14653 INV-005).

field.description:
Dotted field path the append targets (`"summary.0"`, `"output"`,
...); absent means `"text"` (tdd SS4.3.1).

itemId.description: The open item being appended to.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemKind.description:
The eleven v1 item kinds (tdd SS4.5.2–4.5.13) plus post-v1 kinds
(tdd SS4.5.14+). Open: a new kind is additive evolution, and clients
MUST render unknown kinds generically (tdd SS4.10).

ItemReadOutputEncoding.description:
The `item/readOutput` content encoding (tdd SS4.7.4). Closed: text media
is ALWAYS `utf8` and binary media `base64`; a third value would change
the client's decode contract.

ItemReadOutputParams.description:
`item/readOutput` params (tdd SS4.7.4): byte-ranged fetch of stored full
output that the view truncated — the `outputRef` fetch path SS3.9 and
SS4.5.5 owe. Read-only; works on loaded and unloaded sessions; no lease.

itemId.description: The item whose stored output is fetched.

lengthBytes.description:
STORED bytes requested; default and max 6 MiB (tdd SS4.7.4). A value
above the max is served at the max.

offsetBytes.description:
STORED-byte offset to start from; 0 when omitted. STORED bytes are a
property of the output, not of a transport (tdd SS4.7.4).

outputRef.description:
The `outputRef.id` from the item (never the `uri`; the uri is
display/provenance).

sessionId.description: The session the item belongs to.

byteLen.description:
STORED bytes served in THIS response (not the output's total; that is
`outputRef.byteLen` on the item). The next page's `offsetBytes` is
`offsetBytes + byteLen` — short-serving and advancing are separate,
so paging never skips or double-reads a byte (tdd SS4.7.4).

eof.description: `true` when this range reached the end of the stored output.

offsetBytes.description: The STORED-byte offset this response actually served from.

ItemStartedParams.description:
`item/started` params (tdd SS4.3): a new item opened on the transcript.
`sourceRange` is absent when the item opens on an ephemeral record (the
delta-streamed kinds); the item's authoritative open is re-stated by its
durable-sourced `item/completed` (tdd SS4.2).

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from; absent on an
ephemeral-sourced open (spec 14653 INV-009).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemStatus.description:
Item status (tdd SS4.4.1). Open; terminal = anything other than
`"inProgress"`, and unknown values are terminal-unknown, rendered
generically.

ItemUpdatedParams.description:
`item/updated` params (tdd SS4.4.2): an open item changed non-terminally
in a way deltas cannot express — the full item re-emitted at a higher
revision (apply rule: replace iff higher).

item.description: The full item at a higher revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

LastTurn.description:
The last `turn/completed` the session-view fold applied, restated on
`session/resume` and `session/read` so a reopened session can report a
failed last turn (tdd SS2.5.2, ADR 36635 D2/D3).

error.description:
Copied when the `turn/completed` carried it: runtime `failed`
terminals do, host-death `failed` terminals do not (ADR 36635 D2).

reason.description:
Copied when the `turn/completed` carried it; a synthesized host-death
`failed` terminal carries only this (`crash`, `crash_inferred`, or
`incomplete`). Free display text: clients never branch on it.

terminal.description: The turn's terminal (tdd SS4.5.1; open enum).

turnId.description:
The turn's id, as on its `turn/completed`; clients deduplicate a
live `turn/completed` against this member by it (ADR 36635 D2).

LimitKind.description: Quota limit kinds (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50047 D2): open for evolution.

MediaUploadParams.description:
`media/upload` params (tdd SS3.33, ADR 45443 D5): one chunk of a
client-minted upload. All members required.

chunkBase64.description: This chunk's bytes; each call's frame stays in the SS1.1 budget.

commandId.description: One per call; SS3.1.1 replay answers the recorded receipt.

sessionId.description: The session owning the video store.

totalBytes.description: The assembled byte count; must equal the bytes the chunks deliver.

uploadId.description: The client-minted upload id (UUIDv7), sent on every chunk.

MediaUploadResult.description:
`media/upload` result (tdd SS3.33): echoes the client-minted id, on
every chunk and replay.

uploadId.description: The receipt the turn part references.

MessageAttachment.description:
`userMessage` image attachment metadata (tdd SS4.5.2): metadata only —
the durable bytes live in the log and are reachable on the raw altitude.

attachmentId.description:
This attachment's name, `<itemId>/<n>` — the item's id plus this
entry's 1-based position in its `attachments` array (tdd SS4.5.2,
D-071, ADR 42850; #42850). Name only: no link form and no byte read
by id (#42648).

Set by the server on every attachment entry it emits, and identical
on live, paging, snapshot and rebuild paths (tdd SS4.5.2). Optional
in the schema so older servers stay valid; clients compare and store
the whole string and MUST NOT parse it (ADR 42850).

type.description:
Attachment type, `"image"` in v1 (free string: attachment vocabulary
grows additively with the runtime's intake surface).

ModelCatalogEntry.description:
One visible catalog row (tdd SS3.10). Catalog rows marked hidden never
reach the wire, so a client cannot select one.

contextLimit.description: Context limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

cost.description: Cost block; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

defaultReasoningEffort.description:
The row's catalog default. Optional only for decoding older hosts; a
present value is never null and is always a member of `variants`.
Absent under `"unknown"` (ADR 33400 D2).

description.description: Description; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

isActive.description:
Marks the session's effective model when `sessionId` was supplied. May
be false for every row — a client MUST NOT assume exactly one.

isDefault.description: Marks the catalog's default row. May be false for every row.

outputLimit.description: Output limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

profileId.description: Provider profile; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

reasoningEffortVariants.description:
Described selectable tiers, a same-order subset of `variants`.
Optional only for decoding older hosts; a present value is never
null. Absent under `"unknown"` (ADR 33400 D2).

releaseDate.description: Release date; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

variants.description:
Complete ordered selectable efforts. Optional only for decoding older
hosts; a present value is never null. Current hosts always send it.

ModelCatalogSource.description:
Where a model catalog came from (tdd SS3.10). **Open**: an unrecognized
value is an unknown source, not an error.

ModelChangeSource.description: What drove a model selection (tdd SS4.6.1). Open.

ModelCost.description:
Per-1M-token catalog cost, carried **verbatim** for display and never
rounded or re-formatted by the host (tdd SS3.10). Cost arithmetic stays
client-local view math.

currency.description: Currency; nullable — today's catalogs are USD.

ModelDescribedReasoningEffort.description:
One described reasoning-effort tier of a `model/list` row (tdd SS3.10,
ADR 33400 D2): a selectable tier plus the catalog's display string for
it when declared.

description.description:
The catalog's per-tier display string; absent when the catalog
declared none. Optional only for decoding; a present value is never
null.

tier.description: The tier, in the closed D-024 vocabulary.

ModelListParams.description:
`model/list` params (tdd SS3.10): the discovery half of the model-picker
gesture. **A query, not a command** — no `commandId`, no durable intake
record, no view event.

sessionId.description:
When present, the row matching that session's effective model is
flagged `isActive`. When absent, no row is active — a client may list
before it has a session (tdd SS3.10).

ModelListResult.description:
`model/list` result (tdd SS3.10). A snapshot at call time: v1 has no
catalog subscription. `models` MAY be empty — a build shipped with no
bundled models is a supported configuration.

source.description:
Where the catalog came from — how a client tells a live provider
catalog from a test fake and labels it honestly.

ModelReasoningEffortVariants.description: A complete ordered effort set, or an explicit unknown capability.

ModelSelection.description: A model selection (tdd SS3.8). Empty strings are normalized to absent.

profileId.description:
Provider profile. Omitted and explicit `null` both mean "no profile"
(#23468).

ModelVisibleContent.description:
Rich content the model saw beyond text (tdd SS4.5.5,
`ModelVisibleToolContent`): metadata only — fetch bytes via
`item/readOutput` when an `outputRef` exists.

sourceToolName.description: The tool that produced the content.

type.description:
Content type, `"image"` in v1 (free string, grows with the durable
vocabulary).

Notification.description:
A notification frame, either direction (SS1.2 §2.2). No `id`; a
notification is never answered.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty.

OutputRef.description:
Stored-output reference (tdd SS4.5.5): the camelCased fold of the durable
`ToolOutputRef`. The fetch path is `item/readOutput` (#208).

availability.description: Whether the bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5).

kind.description:
The stored output's kind, verbatim durable vocabulary (e.g.
`"tool_output"`; snake_case per the SS1.6 casing exemption).

OutputRefAvailability.description:
Whether a stored output's bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5). Open —
durable runtime vocabulary may grow additively.

PatchSummary.description:
Server-authored edit-family diff summary (tdd SS4.5.5, #33025):
`files` counts the stored patch document's file entries; `added` and
`removed` are the total `+`/`-` prefixed LINE counts summed over the
stored patch's hunks across all files — line counts, never hunk or byte
counts. Rides the `toolCall` item beside `patchRef`; the body is fetched
via `item/readOutput` with `patchRef.id`.

added.description: Total `+`-prefixed line count across all files' hunks.

files.description: File entries in the stored patch document.

removed.description: Total `-`-prefixed line count across all files' hunks.

PendingApprovalPointer.description:
A pending approval in the snapshot: the SS2.5.2 pointer shape plus the
gated `itemId` when one exists (tdd SS4.9.1).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the approval opened at.

PendingRequestKind.description:
The `pendingRequests` discriminator (tdd SS2.5.2). Open enum, v1 values
`approval` and `userInput`.

PendingRequestPointer.description:
A late-joiner pointer at an unsettled server-initiated request
(tdd SS2.5.2, SS2.2.1). The full payloads arrive as re-issued
server-to-client requests right after a `session/resume` response
(tdd SS5.6); `session/read` never re-issues them (tdd SS2.5.5).

**A second E4 instance, RULED with E4 (#22785, owner, 2026-08-26): the
flat discriminated-object precedent is accepted for this type too, on the
`ApprovalSubject` precedent, with the serialized JSON unchanged. A strict
union node kind may be funded later; if it is, it must cover both this
type and `TurnInputPart`.** SS2.5.2 ratifies two
kind-discriminated entry shapes (`{kind: "approval", approvalId,
viewCursor}` / `{kind: "userInput", userInputId, viewCursor}`); this is one
flat object with both ids optional, so the published schema accepts
`{"kind":"approval","userInputId":…}` and an entry carrying no id at all.
The v1 model names no object-variant union (the `ApprovalSubject`
precedent, followed for `TurnInputPart`), and this instance differs from
that one in a way the ruling should see: `kind` here is an OPEN enum,
where `TurnInputPart.type` is closed.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the request opened at.

PendingUserInputPointer.description: A pending user-input prompt in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1, SS5.10).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the prompt opened at.

PlatformFamily.description:
The server runtime's platform family (SS1.4.1); may differ from the
client's. Closed: SS1.4.1 fixes the value set, so widening it is a
deliberate, gate-visible protocol change rather than a silent addition
(a later `Closed`→`Open` flip is itself additive, data-model.md §5.2).

PlatformOs.description:
The server's operating system (SS1.4.1). Closed, for the same reason as
[`PlatformFamily`].

enabled.description:
The record's own install switch; non-enabled rows are included
as `false`, never dropped.

source.description: The installed record's source provenance (ADR 33398 D7 item 3).

PluginChangedParams.description:
`plugin/changed` params (tdd SS3.29.5): an install landed; clients
re-issue `plugin/list` (plus `hook/list` and `skill/list`).

path.description:
The host folder to install from; absolute recommended, relative
resolves against the host working directory.

name.description: The plugin name within the store.

PluginInstallParams.description:
`plugin/install` params (tdd SS3.29.1). Per-session params plus a
client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7) with the uniform SS3.1.1
idempotency contract.

sessionId.description: The target session; its workspace resolves project scope.

PluginInstallResult.description:
`plugin/install` result (tdd SS3.29.1): the SS3.1.2 ack envelope plus
the installed receipt.

warning.description:
The installer's advisory text when the install succeeded with a
caveat; absent otherwise.

PluginInstallScope.description:
The `plugin/install` local-path scope (tdd SS3.29.1). Closed: an
unknown scope is `-32602 invalidParams`.

PluginInstallTarget.description:
The one structured install target (tdd SS3.29.1): a flat object with
two optional arms, exactly one present — the `TurnInputPart`
convention, since the v1 schema model names no object-variant union.
Both arms or neither is `-32602 invalidParams`.

localPath.description: The local-path arm: install from a host folder.

marketplace.description: The marketplace arm: install a named plugin from a store.

PluginListParams.description:
`plugin/list` params (tdd SS3.26.2). Per-session params; rows are the
installed plugin records.

PluginListResult.description:
`plugin/list` result (tdd SS3.26.2): one row per installed plugin
record; the spec promises the set, not an order.

PluginMarketplaceAddParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceAdd` params (tdd SS3.29.2). Per-session params plus
a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

source.description:
The app's source vocabulary: `owner/repo`, a git URL, a `file://`
URL, or a local path.

PluginMarketplaceChange.description:
What happened to a marketplace (tdd SS3.29.6). Closed: an unknown
change is a contract violation, never tolerated.

PluginMarketplaceChangedParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceChanged` params (tdd SS3.29.6): a marketplace was
added, updated, or removed.

pluginCount.description:
The stored record's plugin count; omitted on `removed`, never
fabricated.

skippedCount.description:
The stored record's skipped count; omitted on `removed`, never
fabricated.

PluginMarketplaceRecordResult.description:
The stored marketplace record both add and update answer (tdd
SS3.29.2, SS3.29.3): the SS3.1.2 ack envelope plus the record.

pluginCount.description: The plugins the store now offers.

skipped.description:
Entries the store could not offer, with the reason each was
skipped; empty when nothing was skipped.

PluginMarketplaceRemoveParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceRemove` params (tdd SS3.29.4). Per-session params
plus a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

PluginMarketplaceRemoveResult.description:
`plugin/marketplaceRemove` result (tdd SS3.29.4): the SS3.1.2 ack
envelope plus the removed name.

PluginMarketplaceSourceShape.description: The normalized stored marketplace source (tdd SS3.29.2).

PluginMarketplaceUpdateParams.description:
`plugin/marketplaceUpdate` params (tdd SS3.29.3). Per-session params
plus a client-generated `commandId` (UUIDv7).

PluginSource.description:
A plugin row's source provenance (tdd SS3.26.2, ADR 33398 D7 item 3):
camelCase of `PluginSourceProvenance`. Open (server-produced result
vocabulary, the #22785 enum-openness rule): a future provenance is
additive.

QuotaDetail.description:
Typed quota-exhaustion detail (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50047 D2): the limit
kind plus the provider's reset instant.

limitKind.description: Which quota was exhausted (open enum; unknown values fall back).

resetsAtMs.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the provider says usage resets.

ReasoningEffort.description:
The reasoning-effort tier sampled at submission (tdd SS3.2, SS3.3). The
**same closed tier vocabulary** on both the fresh-turn and steer lanes,
spelled identically; invalid tiers are invalid params. `none` is a tier of
the vocabulary (ask for no reasoning), not a way to say "unset".

ReasoningEffortChangeSource.description:
What drove a reasoning-effort default change (tdd SS4.6.9). Open; v1's
only producer is `user` (an accepted `session/setReasoningEffort`).

ReasoningEffortState.description:
The snapshot's standing session-default reasoning effort (tdd SS4.9.1,
ADR 31255 D1): the fold of the latest completed
`runtime.reasoning_effort_reconfigure` fact — the same pair
`session/reasoningEffortChanged` carries.

reasoningEffort.description:
The standing default tier — the closed SS3.2 vocabulary, spelled
identically to `turn/start.reasoningEffort`.

source.description: Which actor class set the default.

RecapCancelParams.description:
`recap/cancel` params (tdd SS3.28.5): the session plus the cancel's
own retry id. No target — one in-flight slot per session makes the
target unambiguous.

commandId.description: The cancel's own retry id (required, SS3.1.1).

sessionId.description: The session whose in-flight recap to cancel (required).

RecapCancelResult.description:
`recap/cancel` result (tdd SS3.28.5): admission only. In flight →
the recap settles `cancelled`; idle → accepted no-op.

RecapCompletedParams.description:
`recap/completed` params (tdd SS3.28.2): the settlement, delivered
to the requesting connection outside the view stream — no
`viewCursor`, no `sourceRange`. `text` is required on `completed`
(plus optional `title`, untrusted model output — clients MUST
sanitize per spec 442 INV-015); `reason` is required on `failed`;
neither rides `cancelled`/`timedOut`. The struct marks the
conditional members optional; the SS prose pins the per-outcome
rule, the `turn/completed` usage/error convention.

commandId.description: The request's id — the correlation key.

title.description: The model-produced short title (on `completed`, when produced).

RecapFailureReason.description:
`recap/completed` failure reason (tdd SS3.28.2/SS3.28.8): post-ack
failures fold to the single initial value. **Open**: later splits
stay additive (#22785 E2).

RecapOutcome.description:
`recap/completed` outcome (tdd SS3.28.2): the terminal vocabulary,
camelCase per SS1.6. **Open**: a server-produced result vocabulary
(#22785 E2).

RecapRequestParams.description:
`recap/request` params (tdd SS3.28.1): the session plus the
client-minted UUIDv7 retry id. No other param; unknown fields are
`invalidParams`.

RecapRequestResult.description:
`recap/request` result (tdd SS3.28.1): admission only — the ack is
never the recap.

RecordPosition.description:
One end of a [`SourceRange`]: a record's event id and its sequence number
within the stream (tdd SS4.2).

sequence.description: The record's sequence number within its stream.

id.description: Client-chosen id, unique among that client's in-flight requests.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty, never `null`.

RequestId.description:
A request id (SS1.3): client-chosen string or integer. `1` and `"1"` do
not compare equal; each direction owns its own id space.

RequestReceipt.description:
The SS5.3.3 presentation receipt — the client's response to a
server-initiated request (`approval/request`, `userInput/request`).

The response acknowledges presentation only ("a surface showed or will
show this"): it changes no state, the server uses it for diagnostics
alone, and the decision/answer travels as a command (`approval/decide`,
`userInput/answer`). An error response or a dropped connection means this
connection could not present the request; the approval or prompt stays
pending and the request is re-issued on the next subscribe (SS5.6).
There is no dismiss-without-deciding on the wire.

RetractOutcome.description:
A `turn/retracted` settlement outcome (tdd SS4.5.1, ADR 50074 D1).
Open enum (D-033): decode is tolerant — a value outside the list reads
as `Accepted` (the event's historical meaning — pre-feature hosts emit
it only for accepted retracts), never fails. The bundle keeps
enumerating the known values for codegen and docs.

SchemaInfo.description:
The `schema` pair in [`InitializeResult`] (SS1.4.1, SS1.5.3). `version`
is the wire **envelope** schema version — distinct from the session-view
`schemaVersion`, the raw-log `schema_version`, and the 0.x/1.0 stability
posture, which is not on the wire at all (INV-006a).

fingerprint.description:
`sha256:<64 lower hex>` content hash of this server binary's
stable-surface bundle (INV-003). A mismatch is a warning condition,
not an error (SS1.4.1).

version.description:
Envelope schema version; `1` in v1, expected to stay `1` for a long
time (SS1.4.1).

Session.description:
The session object every lifecycle method returns or lists (tdd SS2.4).

Additive-optional evolution applies: clients must ignore unknown fields.

activeTurnId.description:
The `turnId` of the current foreground turn when `status` is
`running`, and `null` when the session is idle (tdd SS2.4).

**Required-nullable, per the owner ruling on #22946** ("approve
required-nullable", review comment `r3863946961`, 2026-08-26). Both
production writers hard-code `"activeTurnId": null`
(`session/start/commit_load.rs` for `session/start`,
`session/snapshot.rs` feeding resume/read/list/fork) and nothing
strips it, so this is what the binary emits and what SS2.4's example
spells. The optional-absent shape published it as plain `string` and
REJECTED every idle `Session` frame the host sent — the #19923 defect
class this PR exists to close.

E5's original evidence for optional-absent ("every committed
transcript shows the omission") was wrong: those transcripts are
hand-authored fixtures, not host recordings. They are corrected in the
same change under the ruling's SS1.5 `regenerationJustification`.

approvalMode.description:
The folded effective approval mode. **Additive-optional**: a Session
object that omits it means the host has not folded a mode, which is
why the index-derived `session/list` entry may legitimately omit it
(tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

attention.description:
Attention flags (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D3). **Additive-optional**,
present only when at least one flag is set; absence is a
NON-assertion (nothing pending, or the loaded session's pending
source declined to answer). Loaded sessions only: a `notLoaded` row
omits it even while its durable pending set is non-empty.

branch.description:
Derived workspace branch (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598) — the index's last
derived value; the live-change signal stays `session/branchChanged`
(SS4.6.4). **Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

createdAt.description:
RFC3339. For a fork this is the fork session id's UUIDv7 mint instant
(tdd SS2.4).

createdByClient.description:
The handshake `ClientInfo` recorded when the session was opened
(FR-003), echoed verbatim — provenance, never an interpretation, and
never a visibility gate (INV-005). **Additive-optional**; absence has
four indistinguishable causes (INV-004): an in-process open; a
pre-#23124 record; a half stamp where only one of name/version was
recorded (FM-005) and `ClientInfo` requires both; and a session with
no admitting handshake of its own — a fork child or a subagent —
which never carries a stamp to begin with.

firstUserPrompt.description:
Derived first-user-prompt preview (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598).
**Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

forkedFrom.description: `null` for root sessions; fork provenance otherwise (tdd SS2.4).

kind.description:
What kind of session this is (spec 42713 FR-001, ADR 42713 D1/D4).
**Open enum**, v1 values `"root"` and `"subagent"`; a client treats an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present kind and renders it, never
rejecting the row. **Additive-optional**: absence asserts nothing —
the host could not determine the home shape (FM-001), or the value is
not yet available to serve (FM-003).

lastActivityAt.description:
Content-activity recency, RFC3339 (tdd SS2.4, ADR 31983 D5).
**Additive-optional**: omitted when no content record exists. Never
advanced by lifecycle bookkeeping (the resume marker, re-stamps) or
a fork's copied seed-replay records, and never precedes `createdAt`.

modelId.description: The winning metadata fold's model; `null` when that record omits it.

name.description:
The durable allocated session name (tdd SS2.4/SS2.14.1, #27598;
ADR 27598 D2/D4). **Additive-optional**: present when the serving path
holds an allocated name, omitted otherwise — absent is never
fabricated. Authoritative and renameable via `session/rename`.

parentSessionId.description:
The containing session's id when `kind` is `"subagent"` (FR-002,
INV-002) — the id of the TOP-LEVEL session whose home holds this
child, which is **not necessarily the session that spawned it**:
native-child homes are physical siblings under the outer session's
`subagent/` directory, so a subagent spawned by another subagent
resolves to the outer session, not to its spawner. A client building
a tree from this field gets one level, not a chain.
Flat rather than nested: there is exactly one fact to
carry, unlike `forkedFrom`'s four-field `ForkProvenance`.
**Additive-optional**; a root carries none.

path.description:
Absolute path of the session's durable log; non-nullable. Under the
ephemeral session profile it is the **empty string**, meaning "no
durable log exists" (tdd SS2.13.2) — the one value a client must not
hand to a filesystem call.

providerId.description: The winning metadata fold's provider; `null` when that record omits it.

sideFrom.description:
`null` for root sessions and forks; side provenance otherwise (tdd
SS2.4/SS2.5.7; ADR 45435 D2). A session carries at most one of
`forkedFrom` and `sideFrom`.

status.description:
Load state as this host knows it; `session/list` reports `notLoaded`
for sessions loaded by *other* hosts (tdd SS2.4).

title.description:
Derived display title (tdd SS2.14.1, #27598): a heuristic that may
evolve — its carriage, not its derivation, is the contract.
**Additive-optional**, omitted when underivable.

turnCount.description: Completed-turn count from the session view fold (tdd SS2.4).

workspaceRoot.description:
The winning metadata fold's workspace root; `null` when that record
omits it — absent is never fabricated (tdd SS2.4).

SessionApprovalModeChangedParams.description:
`session/approvalModeChanged` params (tdd SS5.12): the fold of the
durable approval-mode reconfigure audit fact — every accepted change
writes one; a mode flip without an audit fact is a runtime bug by design.

clientName.description:
The requesting client's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1), recorded on
the audit fact.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionBranchChangedParams.description:
`session/branchChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.4): a durable workspace-branch
observation landed.

branch.description:
The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation — a fact,
not "unchanged" (tdd SS4.6.4).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

vcs.description:
The detected version-control system; absent when no repository was
detected.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionClosedParams.description:
`session/closed` params (tdd SS2.6.2; enrolled by #33065): a loaded
session was unloaded from this host, broadcast to every initialized
connection. After it, the session is `notLoaded`; the log remains on disk
and `session/resume` reloads it. A crash emits nothing — only the two
orderly unload paths do, and both write the durable `SessionEnd` record
first.

viewCursor.description:
The final view head; a client that stores it can later
`session/resume {cursor}` and receive exactly the (empty) suffix. An
**opaque** view cursor: clients relay it, never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

**Required-nullable**: the producers always write the member and
write `null` when the final fold failed at unload (`session/idle.rs`,
`serve/shutdown.rs`; PR #16779 review) — the host defines no cursor
values of its own and never invents one, and the subscriber still
learns the session closed.

SessionClosedReason.description:
The SS2.6.2 closed-reason vocabulary. Server-produced and published
OPEN by owner ruling — the #33065 menu-B pick (PR #33201 comment
5638727249, recorded in the enrollment decision record), which settles
that this notification reason enum publishes open rather than resting on
E2's result-vocabulary rule by analogy. A crash is deliberately not a
reason, because a crash emits no notification at all.

SessionCompactParams.description:
`session/compact` params (tdd SS3.7): manually compact the session's
conversation context — the `/compact` gesture. Compaction runs
asynchronously; the ack is admission only.

turnId.description:
The run whose context to compact. Omit and the server resolves the
session's current/latest run; a session with no resolvable run rejects
with `commandRejected` reason `missing_run` (tdd SS3.7). Any
syntactically valid UUID: a turn from an older session may carry a v4
or v5 id. A malformed id is `invalidParams`.

SessionCompactResult.description:
`session/compact` result (tdd SS3.7). Failures *after* admission
(`summarizer_failed`, `install_rejected`, `cancelled`) are not wire errors
— they arrive as the compaction's terminal view event.

reason.description:
Why the command was a noop, e.g. `no_compactable_history`. Present on
a `noop` status (tdd SS3.7).

SessionConfig.description:
The open configuration extension object shared by `session/start` and
`session/resume` (ADR 32760 D1).

Unknown keys are ignored on the wire, never rejected (tdd SS1.5.4, spec
206 INV-015; D-052 resolving
[#23456](https://github.com/mslsrc/tbh/issues/23456)): the live decoder
is D-042's tolerant path, and TEST-024 keeps every exported bundle free
of `additionalProperties: false`. The Rust typed model's
`deny_unknown_fields` is internal and never exported — the #22785 E6b
closedness export applies nowhere, and the `x-msp-closed` opt-in
mechanism stays inert. Recognized `mcpServers` values are typed and
validated before they leave the wire boundary.

mcpServers.description: Native MCP servers added only to this session runtime.

SessionContextUsageParams.description:
`session/contextUsage` params (tdd SS4.6.6, #14405): context-window
pressure — the counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported
durable fact, joined with the host's pressure basis. Replace wholesale;
emitted only when the `(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple
changes value (identical adoptions emit nothing).

pressure.description: Server-computed pressure level over the basis thresholds.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

usedTokens.description:
Counted-once prompt tokens (#8803) plus output tokens of the driving
record, saturating — the honest occupancy floor.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionDurability.description:
Whether this host writes its sessions to disk (SS1.4.1, SS2.13). A
property of the host process, fixed at construction and identical for
every session and every connection it serves — never requested, granted,
or negotiated, which is why it is not a capability. Open: the
unrepresented degraded state (#14401) has candidate resolutions that add a
third value here, so closed would make that a breaking change.

cutPoint.description:
Copy history through a completed turn, inclusive. Omitted means "all
completed turns" (tdd SS2.5.3).

excludeItems.description:
Skip inline history in the result and page it later — same as
`session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.3).

SessionForkResult.description:
`session/fork` result (tdd SS2.5.3): the `session/resume` envelope for the
**new** session, whose `session.forkedFrom` carries the provenance.

session.description: The new fork session, carrying `forkedFrom` provenance.

viewCursor.description: The new session's view head.

SessionGoalChangedParams.description:
`session/goalChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.2): the projected goal block's
value changed — identical adoptions emit nothing (the change gate), and
an explicit `null` clears. Replace wholesale; `null` never means
unchanged.

goal.description: The full current goal block, or `null` to clear.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionHistory.description:
The `history` envelope shared by `session/resume`, `session/fork`, and
`session/read` (tdd SS2.5.2).

items.description: The full folded item array when `mode` is `inline`; `null` otherwise.

mode.description: What was actually served — never what was asked for (tdd SS2.5.2).

noneReason.description:
Why no history was served — sent exactly when `mode` is `"none"`
(tdd SS2.5.2; D-050, spec 208 INV-19734-1).

snapshot.description:
The folded view state when `mode` is `snapshot` or `anchoredSnapshot`;
`null` otherwise.

SessionKind.description:
What kind of session this is (spec 42713 FR-001/FR-005, ADR 42713 D1/D4).

**Open**: a new kind is additive evolution, and a client MUST render an
unknown value as an unknown-but-present kind rather than rejecting the
row. Both v1 values are terms the tree already uses — the child log
directory is `subagent` and `ItemKind` already carries a `subagent`
variant — so no new vocabulary is minted.

anyOf.description:
1–32 nonempty branch names, each 1–256 UTF-8 bytes, counted before
deduplication; `null` selects sessions with no branch.

SessionListChangedParams.description:
`session/listChanged` params (#33084, ADR 33084 D3): one changed row of
the `session/list` shape — the full SS2.4 Session object as the answering
host's list face serves it at emission (the ADR 29243 live-overlaid row),
a replace, never a delta. Emitted only on connections that negotiated the
`sessionListStream` capability at `initialize` (ADR 33084 D2); row birth
stays on `session/started`, unload pairs with `session/closed`.

session.description: The served list row for the changed session.

SessionListFilter.description:
The `session/list` filter (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-2..5). Members are
ANDed with each other and with the top-level `workspaceRoot` and
`updatedAfter`; values inside each `anyOf` are ORed. The canonical form
the server echoes deduplicates and sorts every set, spells session IDs as
canonical UUIDs, lowercases text terms, and orders `text.fields` `name`
then `title`.

branch.description: Only sessions whose branch is one of these.

sessionId.description: Only sessions whose ID is one of these.

text.description: Only sessions whose served name or title matches these token prefixes.

SessionListParams.description: `session/list` params (tdd SS2.5.4). Read-only; never touches leases.

cursor.description:
Opaque page cursor from a prior result. Page cursors are a distinct
opaque-string family from view cursors and stream cursors, valid only
for re-issuing the same listing (tdd SS2.5.4). Omitted and explicit
`null` both mean "first page" (#23468).

filter.description:
Optional structured selection applied inside the bounded index query
before paging (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-1). Present — including
`{}` — makes a supporting server echo its canonical form as
`appliedFilter`; omitted keeps the pre-#42035 behavior.

limit.description:
Page size; default 50, max 200 — the cap is published under #22785
E6c (owner-ruled 2026-08-26).

updatedAfter.description: Only sessions with log activity after this RFC3339 instant.

workspaceRoot.description: Only sessions whose metadata workspace root equals this path.

appliedFilter.description:
The canonical filter the server applied, present exactly when the
request carried `filter` (#42035, spec 207 FR-42035-1). The probe is
per-predicate PRESENCE (ADR 42035 D6): a client that requires
filtering checks that every predicate it sent comes back as a member
here, and treats a missing member as unsupported. Value equality is
the wrong test — canonicalization trims, lowercases, NFC-normalizes,
dedupes and sorts, so the echoed values often differ from the sent
ones on a correctly filtered page.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; `null` on the last page.

SessionListTextField.description:
A served session field `session/list` text search reads (#42035
FR-42035-3). The client selects it, so the set is closed.

SessionListTextFilter.description:
Name/title token-prefix search (#42035 FR-42035-3/FR-42035-4). Each term
is trimmed, lowercased with ordinary Unicode lowercase, then NFC-
normalized, and matches the beginning of an alphanumeric token,
accent-sensitively (`check` matches `Checkout`; `eck` does not). NFC
means a decomposed and a precomposed spelling of one term are the same
term, and the echo returns the composed form. Matching never reorders
rows.

allOf.description: Every term must match at least one selected field.

anyOf.description:
At least one term must match a selected field. `allOf` plus `anyOf`
carry 1–16 terms in total, each 1–128 UTF-8 bytes in its canonical
form (trimmed, lowercased, NFC) — the bytes `appliedFilter` echoes.
Lowercasing and NFC can both lengthen a term, so a term inside the
bound raw may still exceed it canonically.

SessionMcpServerConfig.description:
One native MCP server supplied at session construction (ADR 32760 D1).

**Closed union** (#33295 owner ruling A1, extending D-033/D-050 to
`oneOf`): a validator MUST reject an undeclared `transport` arm — the
server fails `session/start` decode on an unknown transport, and a future
